items.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006
items.q: Look at Elvis Costello, what he’s doing with this.

ctx.x: Well let me start by saying the creative music community is clearly not as large as straight ahead or traditional jazz is. But New Orleans jazz covers every facet of jazz music which we have heard. And artists, young artists, as they develop for the most part, they really go through those different phases of jazz — playing jazz music until they reach the one that they are most comfortable with and the one that they decide that they want to make a career and play. But then too if you look at Nicholas Payton, so…
Look at Elvis Costello, what he’s doing with this.

Yeah. With Allen Toussaint. You know you just can’t, on any given day it’s kind of like football, on any given day you can’t imagine what or where you may see a New Orleanean playing. Troy “Trombone” Andrews’ roots are in traditional jazz music. I mean he was playing the trombone on the streets of New Orleans in brass bands when he was eight years old, maybe even five, the trumpet was taller than he was. He goes out with Lenny Kravitz now.
